title: Why So Many Numbers Start With 1

vo.text: In real-world numbers, almost a third start with a one. Only about one in twenty start with a nine.
You'd expect every first digit about eleven percent of the time.
Take the first thousand powers of two. Two, four, eight, sixteen, and on.
Pause. How many start with a one?
Three hundred and one. Thirty percent. Nines? Just forty-five.
It's Benford's law. Populations, prices, river lengths: lots of real data does this.
So when someone makes numbers up, the digits come out too even. Auditors check for exactly that.

facts.uses: Benford analysis is a standard forensic-accounting screen for fabricated figures (e.g. Nigrini)
